why: Mine capacity release has ONE mechanism, unlike shells: activeMineIds is an explicit array detonateMine has to prune, where a retired shell simply stops being counted. Drop the prune and a player silently loses a mine slot for the rest of the round -- until a death resets it, which is why the tick-boundary test has to stop at the first round reset to see this at all.
killedBy: detonateMine frees a mine slot when a mine detonates so the player can drop again
standard ordnance limits, driven through step() never exceeds the mine limit, and reuses slots as mines detonate
